sources.title: Malaspina Glacier in a Riot of Color
sources.material_read: HTML article prose and image-acquisition metadata only, before the linked-image failure. No original image pixels read.
sources.identity_basis: Specifically identified27October2023 Landsat9 OLI-2 scene and Earth Observatory article.
sources.actual_usable_scope: Seward supplies the Malaspina glacier; glacier lobes merge on the coastal plain; moraines and coastal lagoon setting are described. This prose is contextual, not proof of the selected foreland link.

correspondence.finding: The selected southwestern opening follows the short feeder valley into the upper Aichilik corridor. The detailed map depicts the feeder turning east and then north into the continuously mapped trunk. The stored line simplifies these bends and is offset onto the valley side; ordinary valley correspondence does not require exact-bank agreement. Glacial or permanent-snow symbols occur upslope to the west, but no selected through-glacier passage is needed or established.

The subsequent northeast and north approach remains within the continuously depicted upper valley, with repeated Aichilik River labels. Side tributaries enter the same trunk; no intervening lake, reservoir or separate-drainage transfer is depicted.

The selected northward corridor follows Aichilik River through mountain-valley bends and widening braided reaches. The western tributary entrance and the nearby Leffingwell Fork approach are distinguishable from the selected northward trunk.

The middle route continues along the labeled Aichilik valley, past the mapped eastern tributary approach and through the northwest bend into the foothill exit. Continuous river and braid-belt depiction establishes the stored joins at ordinary corridor scale.

The long northeast approach follows the lower Aichilik floodplain and reaches its broad braid belt. Kogotpak River is separately labeled on the western side. The selected line generalizes the river corridor; this correspondence does not establish the subsequent eastward transfer across the intervening plain.

correspondence.component_scope: aichilik to egaksrak lateral plain traverse
correspondence.finding: After reaching the Aichilik braid belt, the selected route turns east across the intervening coastal wetland plain toward Egaksrak River, crossing separately depicted small drainage lines. The detailed original does not show a continuous lateral watercourse, linked waterbody chain or mapped junction establishing this selected transfer. Nearby names, wetland coverage and the shared coastal destination cannot supply the missing link.

The last northward river approach lies in the separately labeled Egaksrak River lower braid belt and delta channels. Its local correspondence to the downstream delta is established, independently of the unresolved upstream lateral transfer.

The stored terminal continues into the Egaksrak delta tidal-flat and lagoon-margin complex, southeast of the mapped Beaufort Lagoon label and adjoining the Egaksrak Lagoon setting. The selected endpoint is assessed at that delta/lagoon-margin scale; an exact present-day shoreline, active distributary or marine name boundary is not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: waterbody glacier wetland and managed context
correspondence.finding: The mapped route contains mountain streams, braided river valleys, coastal wetlands and a tidal delta setting. Small lakes and ponds are visible near the coastal delta but no selected through-lake, reservoir or managed-channel connector is established or required in the completed upstream/downstream portions. The material uncertainty is the specific lateral wetland-plain transfer, not a demand to establish current flow, operations or every minor bank.

The selected eastern opening, southwest descent and westward bend lie outside the independently surveyed expedition corridor. No acquired source identifies this selected feeder or proves its continuation into the lower Piura route.

correspondence.component_scope: northern hook and lower river join
correspondence.finding: The selected northern hook and southward approach precede the securely recognized Tabanco corridor. The acquired regional maps do not establish the actual selected feeder-to-river join.
The expedition route and its Tabanco discussion identify the southward lower Piura passage toward the Ramón wetland complex at ordinary corridor scale.

The mapped survey traverses the Ramón wetland, with documented river branches and reconnection. The selected passage lies in this connected lake corridor; no claim is made that every mapped branch bears the river name.

The survey explicitly continues from Ramón through the Sánchez, Tres Brazos and Peñal setting toward Las Salinas. This supports the selected connecting corridor without asserting present hydraulic operations.
Both inspected map publications identify Las Salinas/Salinas here. The field survey crosses the lake to its southern outlet setting, supporting an internal lake passage at ordinary scale.

A regional connection is documented, but the expedition took the southern Zapayal approach after unsuccessful entries at Palo Parado and Garita García. The selected more direct approach is not resolved by the acquired maps; the alternative surveyed route is not substituted for it.
The western part is within the mapped Virrilá estuary corridor. Its connection from the selected eastern approach remains dependent on the unresolved entry choice.

correspondence.component_scope: virrila main estuary and northern turn
correspondence.finding: MINAM Map11b depicts the continuous east-west estuary and its northern turn toward the coast. The selected internal estuary passage is supported at ordinary waterbody scale.

The stored last segment heads northwest from the estuary toward Bahía de Sechura. MINAM depicts the estuary mouth by Parachique, but does not establish this selected shore crossing. The expedition ends at Puente Virrilá and cannot independently close the terminal. Neither its endpoint nor another Piura mouth replaces the stored terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southern opening and northeast foothill course
correspondence.finding: The conservation plan places a multi-branched Big Fish River watershed west of Aklavik and includes Canoe Lake in its site description. Its management-area and riparian overlay does not distinguish the selected initial feeder from neighboring upper branches or demonstrate the selected eastward connection. This part lies west of the independently read Aklavik land-use sheet's coverage. No actual selected lake passage is established by the mention of Canoe Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Central northward course and westward bend
correspondence.finding: The community map shows the Big Fish site extending from the foothills toward the western delta. Its broad colored riparian polygons cover the river corridors; they do not supply continuously readable source linework for the chosen northward, west-bending and renewed northward route. The actual intermediate joins remain unestablished. No distinct tributary name is assigned from this generalized watershed portrayal.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast approach to delta channel network
correspondence.finding: Aklavik107B directly depicts a lower Big Fish River label near the western map edge and the neighboring Moose, West and Tiktalik channel network south of Shallow Bay. Its eastern portion is consistent with the selected delta-side approach, but the course preceding the sheet edge and the complete chosen approach-to-channel join are not demonstrated by the acquired coverage. The earlier fisheries-plan prose independently recognizes the Big Fish River mouth in the Mackenzie Delta; a mouth reference alone is not proof of this selected connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest delta passage and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The land-use original labels Shallow Bay and shows the wetland-rich southern delta channel network. ARC403 states that Tiktalik Channel on the southwest side of Shallow Bay connects with West Channel. The community plan separately identifies the Mackenzie Bay and Shallow Bay conservation site. Together these support the receiving setting and ordinary named-channel relationship, but not the entire selected northwest passage beyond the land-use sheet's western edge or its chosen final channel-to-bay connection. The selected bayward extension cannot itself supply independent source proof.

The lower source map depicts extensive wetlands, ponds and branching delta channels. No discrete selected reservoir, dam, canal or glacier passage is established from the materials read. Canoe Lake is part of the community site's description but is not proved to be traversed by the selected route. Missing upper and delta through-links remain substantive evidence gaps rather than precise-bank or current-operation questions.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen canadian opening and upper ice corridor
correspondence.finding: The Canadian opening lies in the broad upper Seward ice corridor south of the Mount Logan massif. The Sentinel-1 scene in Figure7a depicts its long eastward course and the southward bend at the eastern end. This supplies geographic ice-corridor correspondence for all42 stored parts, without asserting a natural surface river or reproducing the paper’s modeled glacier-flow lines as measured water channels. USGSTopo is blank on this Canadian reach.

The SAR scene and overlapping federal cartography depict the southward glacier passage across the border, the narrowing between adjacent mountain spurs, and the opening into Malaspina Glacier beside the Hitchcock Hills. The whole selected middle fragment and both stage-boundary joins have geographic ice-corridor correspondence. No natural-river name or mapped liquid-water path is established across the ice.

The initial lower-stage section runs east around the southern Hitchcock Hills and then southeast through the mapped eastern Malaspina ice-margin setting. The local small lake and hill-side streams remain separate components rather than evidence of one river named Malaspina. The SAR scene supplies broader glacier-terrain context.

correspondence.component_scope: ice margin to first foreland stream gap
correspondence.finding: Between the eastern Malaspina ice-margin approach and the first continuously depicted stream entering the northeastern Malaspina Lake margin, the selected line crosses a ridged, pond-rich foreland. The federal map does not depict a continuous connecting channel over this interval. The regional SAR scene identifies glacier/debris terrain but does not establish this selected drainage through-link. This is a substantive connection gap, not a demand for exact contemporary glacier margins, banks, water levels or vertex agreement.

correspondence.component_scope: mapped foreland stream lake entry and join
correspondence.finding: Once the depicted foreland stream begins, its channel and wetland-expanded reach can be followed into the northeastern margin of Malaspina Lake and to the lake outlet corridor. The selected tributary junction is in this connected lake-margin setting. These observations do not bridge the separately identified upstream foreland gap.

All six selected parts lie across the southern island-and-peninsula margin of Malaspina Lake. This is a generalized lake-crossing component, not an independently established river with the name Malaspina. Its opening and continuation into the next selected tributary stage are within the same depicted lake complex.

All five parts continue east through Malaspina Lake toward the northeastern lake-margin/outlet junction with the selected mainstem. The open-water lake passage, continuation from the preceding tributary stage and receiving connection are depicted. The stored tributary role is retained without inventing a separately named tributary river.

correspondence.component_scope: coastal outlet and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The eastern lake outlet continues through the broad coastal channel to the selected terminal immediately inside the ocean-side barrier. The map labels Sudden Stream and Kame Stream in this outlet area, with the smaller Kame approach entering the coastal channel from the west. These are bounded outlet-reach/locality names, not names for the full glacier-to-coast selection. The terminal is geographically accounted for in the coastal outlet; no exact tidal limit, present shoreline or extension beyond the stored endpoint is assigned.
